title: Zero-variable stabilization of a localized conormal module
statement: Let R and A be commutative rings with an R-algebra structure on A, a ∈ A, and P₀ a polynomial presentation of A over R with n₀ variables and m₀ relations [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. For each natural number r there exists a presentation P of A over R with exactly n₀+r variables and m₀+r relations and an A_a-linear equivalence A_a tensor_A Cotangent(P) ≃ (A_a tensor_A Cotangent(P₀)) × (Fin r → A_a), where Cotangent means the kernel modulo its square with the quotient A-action, and A_a is localization away from a [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. No smoothness, nontriviality, or conormal freeness assumption is required.

source.place: Tag 07EZ, proof of (e), paragraph adjoining r zero variables; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07EZ read 2026-10-13

proof.text: Construct Q presenting A as an A-algebra on Fin r zero-valued variables with relations X_i. Prove by polynomial induction that p-C(eval₀ p) lies in the ideal generated by X_i. A polynomial in the kernel has eval₀ p=0, so this proves the relation-span equality. The Jacobian matrix is identity; Mathlib SubmersivePresentation.cotangentEquiv identifies its conormal module with Fin r → A.

Compose Q with P₀ by Presentation.comp. Mathlib Generators.Cotangent.exact and Cotangent.surjective_map_ofComp give the exact sequence A tensor_A Cotangent(P₀) → Cotangent(Q.comp P₀) → Cotangent(Q) → 0. Define the generator homomorphism back by setting new variables to zero and leaving old variables unchanged. Its composite with toComp is the identity. Extension.Cotangent.map_comp and TensorProduct.lid therefore show that the induced conormal map, followed by the inverse tensor-unit map, retracts the first map. Function.Exact.splitInjectiveEquiv splits this exact sequence. Identify the factors using TensorProduct.lid and Q.cotangentEquiv.

Reindex variables by the equivalence Fin(n₀+r) ≃ Fin r ⊕ Fin n₀ obtained from finSumFinEquiv and sumComm, and relations similarly. The inverse variable renamings define generator homomorphisms with identity composites, so Extension.Cotangent.map_comp and map_id induce a conormal linear equivalence. Base change this equivalence to B=A_a by LinearEquiv.baseChange. TensorProduct.prodRight distributes tensor over the two factors; TensorProduct.piScalarRight identifies B tensor_A (Fin r → A) with Fin r → B. These constructions are valid for empty variable or relation sets and for zero rings.

proof_origin.place: Detailed reconstruction of Tag 07EZ proof (e) using the already-proved Mathlib composed-conormal exact sequence and its explicit zero-evaluation retraction.

mathlib_searches.query: The conormal module of a polynomial presentation after adjoining variables mapped to zero is the product of the original conormal module and a free module
A polynomial presentation with extra variables sent to zero has cotangent module equal to the old cotangent module plus a free module
mathlib_searches.verdict: Related results only. The basis-presentation theorem adds an invertible variable and requires an unlocalized conormal basis, so it does not give fixed-size zero-variable stabilization.
Usable component: combined in the proved Lean implementation with a zero-evaluation retraction and the zero-variable presentation conormal equivalence.

from.place: Essential-surjectivity approximation, Tag 07EZ proof (e): replacement by a presentation with r additional variables sent to zero.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_zero_variable_presentation_localized_cotangent_equiv
    (R : Type u) (A : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    (a : A) {n₀ m₀ : ℕ} (P₀ : Presentation R A (Fin n₀) (Fin m₀)) (r : ℕ) :
    ∃ (P : Presentation R A (Fin (n₀ + r)) (Fin (m₀ + r))), Nonempty
      ((Localization.Away a ⊗[A] P.toExtension.Cotangent) ≃ₗ[Localization.Away a]
        ((Localization.Away a ⊗[A] P₀.toExtension.Cotangent) ×
          (Fin r → Localization.Away a)))
